$comment: Single source of truth for the required payment posture: customer-facing checkout methods, build-time VITE_* gates and server runtime gates. Vite flags can silently hide a method and runtime flags can silently disable execution, webhooks or renewals. Staging and confirmed-production builds, the production env-plan parity test and deployed-bundle proof all read THIS reviewed contract. Changing a required rail or method therefore requires a git change; a dashboard edit cannot quietly remove card/wallet, Tpay one-time or Model O subscription payments. See scripts/payment-ui-contract.ts.

Stripe card/wallet plus initial Tpay BLIK code that registers a Model O PAYID mandate. Pay-By-Link is one-time only and must never appear here.

providers.label: Stripe (Karta / Apple Pay / Google Pay)
providers.comment: The visibility TOGGLE is forwarded from git (deploy workflow + deploy-hidden-preview.sh) so it is single-sourced + reviewed, like Tpay. VITE_STRIPE_PUBLISHABLE_KEY stays an environment-specific value in the Vercel project env (test key on staging, live key on prod) — it is a credential value, not a toggle — but is still asserted non-empty in the built bundle.

providers.label: Tpay (BLIK z kodem / Pay-By-Link / BLIK Model O)
providers.$scopeComment: Production requires Tpay BLIK-code and PBL for one-time checkout plus BLIK Model O activation for subscriptions. Saved-alias one-click remains a distinct optional UI and stays forbidden on production until its own application evidence exists.

$forbiddenFlagsComment: The mirror image of providers[].requiredVisibleIn. Those entries prove a payment method is VISIBLE where it must be; these prove one is NOT visible where it must not be. Both are enforced against the built bundle by scripts/payment-ui-contract.ts, so the same assertion guards the staging deploy (--assert-deploy), the production cutover (release-production.yml), and PR CI (--assert-dist). A flag listed here must be absent or bake anything other than 'true'; being in config/production-env-plan.json `unset` is the intended way to satisfy it, but this reads the OUTPUT, so an out-of-band Vercel dashboard value cannot slip past — the same reason the positive direction exists (CJ01-H).

forbiddenFlags.reason: Staging fake-payment simulator. On production it would offer customers a checkout path that never takes real money — an order that looks paid and is not.

Saved-alias one-click is distinct from initial Model O activation. Keep it hidden until its own application/webhook/ledger evidence exists; Model O subscriptions start with an ordinary six-digit BLIK code.
